clinical.citation: Rolandic epilepsies CNV study - A subset of genomic alterations detected in rolandic epilepsies contains candidate or known epilepsy genes including GRIN2A and PRRT2 (PMID: 24372385)

variants.description: Rare CNV (microdeletion/microduplication) comprising or disrupting PRKCE; exact coordinates and copy-number state not given in abstract
phenotypes: Possible cognitive, speech, language, reading or behavioral comorbidity (not specified for this patient)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was listed among strong candidate genes for epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders disrupted by rare CNVs. The authors state that only a subset of the CNVs may contribute to the phenotype, and inheritance for this CNV is not specified in the abstract.

clinical.citation: Contiguous gene deletion of chromosome 2p16.3-p21 as a cause of Lynch syndrome (PMID: 28555354)

variants.description: 4.8 Mb heterozygous deletion at 2p16.3-p21 (SNP array) spanning MSH2, MSH6, EPCAM, NRXN1, CALM2, FBXO11, PRKCE and other genes
phenotypes: Synchronous sigmoid adenocarcinoma with MSH2/MSH6 loss

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Lynch syndrome was attributed to deletion of MSH2, MSH6 and EPCAM. PRKCE was only one of many co-deleted genes, so its specific contribution is unknown. Family history was unrevealing.

clinical.citation: ASHG 2018 - A copy number variation map of pediatric neuropsychiatric traits

variants.description: Rare CNVs affecting PRKCE (details not specified)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was named as one of the genes driving the OCD-trait association signal in the burden and locus analyses of rare CNVs and SNVs/indels. This is a statistical association, not individual-level pathogenicity.

clinical.diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was among the nuclear-encoded mitochondrial-related genes tested with the TADA-denovo model for excess de novo variants. The PRKCE row is not clearly a prioritized gene, and no per-patient phenotyping is given.

clinical.citation: Construction of copy number variation landscape and characterization of associated genes in a Bangladeshi cohort of neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 36959829)

variants.description: Rare CNV(s) encompassing PRKCE, listed among 18 critical-exon genes in smaller CNVs

clinical.diagnostic_reason: PRKCE was a critical-exon gene (gene constraint metric) located within pathogenic or VUS CNVs. It was not prioritized as a candidate, because PSMC3 was selected instead.

global PKCε knockout bone marrow-derived macrophages also tested for lipid retention and cytokine secretion

phenotypes: reduced α4 nAChR subunit phosphorylation in synaptosomes
more severe and prolonged sazetidine-A-induced hypothermia

phenotypes: decreased conditioned place preference for nicotine
reduced α6 and β3 nicotinic receptor subunit mRNA in ventral midbrain and striatum
deficit in cholinergic modulation of dopamine release in nucleus accumbens

phenotypes: PKCε inhibitors reduced ethanol consumption in wild-type but not Prkce-/- mice
off-target locomotor impairment and prolonged loss of righting recovery persisted in Prkce-/- mice

phenotypes: protected from high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance (normal glucose and insulin at 1 week)
increased liver triacylglycerol in fat-fed mice
altered hepatic lipid partitioning with increased fatty acid esterification
no fat-diet-induced rise in oxygen consumption or liver mitochondrial respiration
reduced ROS production in hepatocytes with palmitate
increased glucose-stimulated insulin secretion after 16 weeks of fat feeding

phenotypes: reduced liver 4-hydroxyproline and aspartate, increased glutamate
better maintenance of blood glucose on fasting
lower liver and plasma lipids on fasting
smaller reduction in fat pad mass on fasting

model_organism.citation: Diverse roles for protein kinase C delta and protein kinase C epsilon in the generation of high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance in mice: regulation of lipogenesis by protein kinase C delta (PMID: 19809797)
phenotypes: protected against high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance via enhanced insulin availability

biological.citation: Wang et al. 2021 - FAIM regulates autophagy through glutaminolysis in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 34720024)
biological.summary: FAIM promotes GAC (glutaminase C) tetramer formation by increasing PRKCE/PKCε-mediated phosphorylation of GAC. This raises α-ketoglutarate production and activates MTOR, suppressing autophagy. PKCε therefore acts as a GAC kinase within the glutaminolysis–MTOR–autophagy axis in lung adenocarcinoma cells.

biological.citation: SHORT syndrome due to a novel de novo mutation in PRKCE (Protein Kinase Cɛ) impairing TORC2-dependent AKT activation (PMID: 28934384)
biological.summary: A de novo PRKCE variant was found by exome sequencing in a child with SHORT syndrome who had no PIK3R1 mutation. Kinase assays showed partial loss of function. The mutant kept its PDK1 and SIN1 interactions, but bound SIN1 with higher affinity and had altered mTORC2-dependent priming. It impaired mTORC2-dependent pAKT-S473, and patient lymphoblasts showed reduced pFOXO1-S256 and pS6-S240/244.
biological.sample_size: 1 proband plus parents; patient lymphoblastoid cell lines, HEK293 cells

biological.citation: Maternal Prkce expression in mature oocytes is critical for the first cleavage facilitating maternal-to-zygotic transition in mouse early embryos (PMID: 35582855)
biological.summary: Prkce transcript level in mature oocytes correlates with 2-cell rate across inbred mouse strains. Prkce knockout oocytes had a reduced 2-cell rate (32.4% vs 80.1%), which Prkce cRNA injection rescued (76.7%). Knockout caused 143 DEGs enriched for cell cycle regulation.

biological.citation: Time-dependent effects of Prkce deletion on glucose homeostasis and hepatic lipid metabolism on dietary lipid oversupply in mice (PMID: 21347625)
biological.summary: Prkce-/- mice were protected from high-fat-diet-induced glucose intolerance. Early protection was linked to altered hepatic lipid partitioning (increased esterification, higher liver triacylglycerol), lack of diet-induced mitochondrial oxygen consumption and reduced ROS. Later protection was linked to enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-146a targets PRKCE to modulate papillary thyroid tumor development (PMID: 23457043)
biological.summary: A luciferase reporter assay confirmed that miR-146a directly binds the PRKCE 3'-UTR. miR-146a overexpression lowered PKCε levels in NPA-187 PTC cells and increased apoptosis. It also inhibited xenograft tumor growth, implicating PKCε in Ras/Raf-1 signaling, anti-apoptosis and NF-κB feedback.

biological.citation: miR-21-5p/PRKCE axis implicated in immune infiltration and poor prognosis of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (PMID: 36186442)
biological.summary: PRKCE expression is decreased in KIRC tumors compared with normal tissue, and low expression is associated with poor survival and advanced stage. High PRKCE promoter methylation and miR-21-5p may explain the low expression. PRKCE overexpression suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion of ACHN and Caki-1 cells, and PRKCE correlates with immune infiltration.
biological.sample_size: TCGA/GEO cohorts; ACHN and Caki-1 cells

biological.citation: Fetal exposure to cocaine causes programming of Prkce gene repression in the left ventricle of adult rat offspring (PMID: 18945988)
biological.summary: Prenatal cocaine decreased Prkce mRNA in the left ventricle of adult male offspring. Methylation of the Sp1 binding sites (-346 and -268) in the Prkce promoter increased, which reduced SP1 binding. Reporter assays showed these Sp1 sites strongly stimulate Prkce promoter activity, so the repression is epigenetic.

biological.citation: DNA methylation analysis in nonalcoholic fatty liver disease suggests distinct disease-specific and remodeling signatures after bariatric surgery (PMID: 23931760)
biological.summary: PRKCE showed NAFLD-specific DNA methylation and mRNA expression differences in liver. This was replicated by bisulfite pyrosequencing, and PRKCE is grouped with insulin/IGF signaling genes (IGF1, IGFBP2).

biological.citation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of genetic association studies for the role of inflammation and the immune system in diabetic nephropathy (PMID: 28616206)
biological.summary: In a meta-analysis of genetic association studies, PRKCE variants were associated with increased risk of diabetic nephropathy.
biological.sample_size: 103 association studies in the review overall

biological.citation: Genes associated with cognitive performance in the Morris water maze: an RNA-seq study (PMID: 33328525)
biological.summary: Hippocampal Prkce expression was higher in high-performing than low-performing Morris water maze mice. It is grouped with AMPA receptor signaling and glutamatergic transmission/LTP genes.
